'''Kameshwar C. Wali''' (October 15, 1927 – January 14, 2022) was an Indian-born American theoretical physicist who was the Distinguished Research Professor of Physics Emeritus at [[Syracuse University]]'s [[Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences|College of Arts and Sciences]]. He was a specialist in [[high energy physics]], particularly symmetries and dynamics of [[elementary particles]], and the author of ''Chandra: A Biography of S. Chandrasekhar'' and ''Cremona Violins: a physicist's quest for the secrets of Stradivari''.

== Early life and education==
Wali was born at [[Bijapur]] in the state of [[Karnataka]], India, in 1927. He was the seventh of ten children (three of whom died in infancy). His father, a civil servant in the British Colonial system, moved the family to [[Belgaum]].<ref name="phyinterviews.syr">{{Cite web|url=http://phyinterviews.syr.edu/media/pdfs/Kameshwar%20C.%20Wali.pdf|title=Goldberg, Joshua N. Department of Physics Interview Archive: Kameshwar Wali|access-date=30 May 2014|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304080752/http://phyinterviews.syr.edu/media/pdfs/Kameshwar%20C.%20Wali.pdf}}</ref>

In 1944 Wali enrolled at the Raja Lakhamagouda Science Institute in Belgaum, newly founded by the [[Karnatak Lingayat Education Society]] (KLES) and inaugurated by the Sir [[C.V. Raman]]. He obtained his BSc with distinction in physics in 1948 and was appointed a lecturer in physics at the college before going on, in 1950, to commence post-graduate studies at [[Banaras Hindu University]] (BHU).<ref name="phyinterviews.syr"/> He received his MSc in physics in 1952, specializing in spectroscopy, and was appointed a lecturer in the Science College.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|title=Home - Unit - FHPP|url=https://engage.aps.org/fhpp/home|access-date=2022-02-06|website=engage.aps.org|language=en|archive-date=6 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206015106/https://engage.aps.org/fhpp/home}}</ref> While teaching, he pursued independent studies for an MA in mathematics and received it in 1954. He was awarded the Chancellor's Gold Medal—the University's highest honor.<ref name="phyinterviews.syr"/>

In 1955, Wali travelled to the United States to join the PhD program in physics at the [[University of Wisconsin, Madison]]. His advisor and mentor was [[Robert G. Sachs]], later the associate director of the high-energy physics division at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hildebrand |first1=Roger |last2=Winstein |first2=Bruce |last3=wali |first3=Kameshwar |title=Robert Green Sachs |journal=Physics Today |date=August 1999 |volume=52 |issue=8 |pages=79–81 |doi=10.1063/1.882795 |doi-access= }}</ref> In 1959, Wali was joined in America by his wife and three daughters. Wali obtained his doctorate in 1959.<ref name="phyinterviews.syr"/>

== Career ==
Wali became a research associate at [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1960. In 1962 he joined [[Argonne National Laboratory]], [[Illinois]], as an assistant scientist in the Physics Division.<ref name="auto"/> The following year he joined the newly created High Energy Physics division at Argonne as an associate scientist. In 1967 he was promoted to senior scientist.<ref name="syr faculty page"/> Concurrently he taught courses at [[Northwestern University]] (1964–1966) and at the [[University of Chicago]] (1967–1969). He was a visiting scientist at the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]], at [[Trieste]], Italy (1967).<ref name="SU Obit"/>

In 1969, Wali joined the faculty of the [[Syracuse University]] physics department as full professor, a position he held until his retirement in 1998.<ref name="SU Obit"/> Wali became the head of the High Energy Theory group in 1969.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Catterall |first1=Simon |last2=Hubisz |first2=Jay |last3=Balachandran |first3=Aiyalam |last4=Schechter |first4=Joe |title=Elementary Particle Physics at Syracuse. Final Report |url=https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1095082 |access-date=26 February 2021 |publisher=Syracuse Univ., NY (United States) |date=5 January 2013 |language=English}}</ref> He served as chairman of the physics department from 1986 to 1989, and was the Joel Dorman Steele Professor at Syracuse between 1997–98.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Enslin |first1=Rob |title=SU's Mark Bowick to Be Honored as New Steele Professor Oct. 31 |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2013/10/18/sus-mark-bowick-to-be-honored-as-new-steele-professor-oct-31-82904/ |access-date=16 May 2019 |work=SU News |publisher=[[Syracuse University]] |date=18 October 2013}}</ref>

He was project director of the Elementary Particle Theory Group, DOE from 1969 to 1993. He has been on the International Advisory Committee for PASCOS (Particles, Strings and Cosmology) Conference since its inception in 1994. During his sabbatical leaves, he was visiting scientist at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] (IHES), [[Bures-sur-Yvette]], France (Fall 1971, 1975, 1979, 1983, and Spring 1990); associate of the physics department, [[Harvard University]] (from 1982); visiting scientist, [[University of Chicago]] (Summer 1985); Dozor Visiting Fellow, [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]], [[Beer-Sheva]], [[Israel]] (Jan-Feb 1993); and senior scholar, [[Fulbright Foundation]], Australia (Jan-May 1995).<ref name="syr faculty page"/> As a member of the United States and [[Vietnam]] Research Collaboration, Wali visited [[Hanoi, Vietnam|Hanoi]] in 1979 and 1989 for establishing research contacts and to present lectures.<ref name="auto"/>

Wali retired in 1998, and became a Distinguished Research Professor Emeritus at Syracuse University.<ref name="SU Obit">{{cite news |last1=Bernardi |first1=Dan |title=Arts and Sciences Remembers Longtime Physics Professor Kameshwar C. Wali |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2022/02/08/arts-and-sciences-remembers-longtime-physics-professor-kameshwar-c-wali/ |access-date=17 February 2022 |work=Syracuse University News |date=8 February 2022}}</ref>

==Research==
His specific research contributions include:<ref name="syr faculty page">{{cite web|title=Kameshwar Wali|url=http://www.phy.syr.edu/research/relativity/Wali/index.html|access-date=12 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528194122/http://www.phy.syr.edu/research/relativity/Wali/index.html|archive-date=28 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.phy.syr.edu/research/hetheory/wali.html |title=Wali: Research |access-date=14 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525032449/http://www.phy.syr.edu/research/hetheory/wali.html |archive-date=25 May 2012 }}</ref>
* Electromagnetic structure of the [[nucleon]], providing a combination of the conventional [[Dirac equation|Dirac]] and [[Pauli equation|Pauli]] form factors as proper [[Fourier transform]]s of spatial charge and magnetization inside the nucleon.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ernst |first1=F. J. |last2=Sachs |first2=R. G. |last3=Wali |first3=K. * Theoretical considerations in exploring the spin and decay properties of new elementary particles being discovered.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sawyer |first1=R. F. |last2=Wali |first2=K. C. |title=Pion-Pion Interactions in τ and τ′ Decays |journal=[[Physical Review]] |date=15 August 1960 |volume=119 |issue=4 |pages=1429–1435 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.119.1429 |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.119.1429 |access-date=17 February 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Feldman |first1=G. |last2=Fulton |first2=T. |last3=Wali |first3=K. C. |last2=Warnock |first2=Robert L. |title=Breaking of SU(3) Symmetry in the 3+/2 Meson-Baryon Decouplet. |journal=Physical Review |date=21 September 1964 |volume=135 |issue=6B |pages=B1358–B1368 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.135.B1358 |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.135.B1358 |access-date=17 February 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Contributions to the history of physics==
Wali is a founding member of the Forum on the History of Physics within the [[American Physical Society]]. He wrote the authoritative biography of the astrophysicist [[Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name="syr faculty page"/><ref>{{cite web|title=History of Physics Newsletter|url=http://www.aps.org/units/fhp/newsletters/upload/spring06.pdf|access-date=1 January 2014}}</ref> ''Chandra: A Biography of S. Chandrasekhar'' (published in 1991 by The [[University of Chicago Press]]),<ref>{{Cite book | url = https://archive.org/details/chandrabiography0000wali | url-access = registration | title = Chandra: A Biography of S. Chandrasekhar | publisher = [[University of Chicago Press]] | isbn = 978-0-226-87055-7 | last1 = Wali | first1 = Kameshwar C | year = 1991}}</ref> complemented by subsequent articles and books on Chandra: ''S Chandrasekhar: The Man Behind The Legend'', and ''A Quest for Perspectives: Selected Works of S Chandrasekhar''. He also edited Chandrasekhar's scientific journals, which were published in ''A Scientific Autobiography, S Chandrasekhar'' (2010).<ref>Wali, K.S. 2010. ''A Scientific Autobiography, S. Chandrasekhar''. World Scientific (2010), {{ISBN|978-981-4299-57-2}}</ref>

His other books include ''Cremona Violins: A Physicist's Quest for Secrets of [[Stradivari]]'' ({{ISBN|978-9812791108}}) and ''[[Satyendra Nath Bose]]—His Life and Times: Selected Works''. ({{ISBN|978-9812790712}})

*In 2008 a dedicated Kameshwar C. Wali Lecture in the Sciences and Humanities at Syracuse University was established by Wali's daughters, Alaka, Achala and Monona.<ref name="2022 lecture"/> The inaugural lecture, ''Evolution and Symbiosis: Memoirs of Planet Earth'', was given by [[Lynn Margulis]].{{citation needed|date=January 2020}} Subsequent lectures in the series have been given inter alia by [[Janna Levin]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Campaign News &#124; Forever Orange|url=https://giving.syr.edu/news/index.html|access-date=2022-02-06|website=giving.syr.edu}}</ref> [[George Packer]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://asnews.syr.edu/newsevents_2010/releases/wali_lecture.html|title=George Packer on Afghanistan and Vietnam|access-date=14 January 2014|archive-date=14 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140114193818/http://asnews.syr.edu/newsevents_2010/releases/wali_lecture.html}}</ref> [[Ian Shipsey]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=2011-09-28|title=SU Humanities Center, physics department team up for Wali Lecture Oct. 6 &#124; Syracuse University News|url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2011/09/28/ian-shipsey/|access-date=2022-02-06|language=en-US}}</ref> [[Arthur Zajonc]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://asnews.syr.edu/newsevents_2013/releases/2013_Wali_Lecture.html |title=Arthur Zajonc lectures on Science and the Dalai Lama |access-date=14 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140114193808/http://asnews.syr.edu/newsevents_2013/releases/2013_Wali_Lecture.html |archive-date=14 January 2014 }}</ref> [[Diane Ackerman]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://asnews.syr.edu/newsevents_2013/releases/diane_ackerman_lecture.html|title=Diane Ackerman on the subversive power of compassion|access-date=14 January 2014|archive-date=14 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140114193814/http://asnews.syr.edu/newsevents_2013/releases/diane_ackerman_lecture.html}}</ref> and [[Abhay Ashtekar]].<ref name="2022 lecture">{{cite news |last1=Bernardi |first1=Dan |title=Annual Wali Lecture Will Honor the Life and Legacy of Physics Professor Kameshwar C. Wali |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2022/11/01/annual-wali-lecture-will-honor-the-life-and-legacy-of-physics-professor-kameshwar-c-wali/ |access-date=11 November 2022 |work=Syracuse University News |date=1 November 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Wali married Kashi Kulkarni in May 1952. She was a fellow student at BHU doing her MSc in physics.

At Syracuse, he befriended writers [[Tess Gallagher]] and [[Raymond Carver]].<ref name="SU Obit"/>

He died in [[Syracuse, New York]], on January 14, 2022, at the age of 94.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bernardi |first1=Dan |title=A&S Remembers Kameshwar C. Wali, Longtime Physics Professor and Friend of Both the Sciences and Humanities at Syracuse University |url=https://thecollege.syr.edu/news-all/news-from-2022/as-remembers-kameshwar-c-wali-longtime-physics-professor-and-friend-of-both-the-sciences-and-humanities-at-syracuse-university/ |access-date=6 February 2022 |work=[[Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences]] |date=January 27, 2022 |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Kameshwar Wali |url=https://obits.syracuse.com/us/obituaries/syracuse/name/kameshwar-wali-obituary?id=32255651 |publisher=[[Syracuse Post Standard]] |access-date=25 January 2022}}</ref>
